newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK May PMI services survey.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK May PMI services survey.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to the UK May PMI services survey, which showed the largest rise yet in the business activity index.
The index rose to 64.8 from 61.2 in April.
"I think the evidence is piling up for a rate increase. It's in line with the PMI for manufacturing...which showed domestic conditions are so buoyant that it is offsetting weakness in manufacturing."
MARIAN BELL, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND
"This is a repeat of last month's survey and it is quite clear Bank of England thinks rates need to go up further."
"Historically, inflation is low and projected to stay quite low. But we are in a cyclical upturn and cost pressures have been noted. A monetary tighening is needed."

"The survey indicates an accelerating service sector with some increase in price pressures. Looking through the data. it's hard to find any areas of softness. Consequently, it adds to pressure for a rate increase on Friday. We'll only get two outside members actually voting on Friday. They've got no chance of stopping the Bank if it wants a rate rise. But my guess is they will go with the consensus anyway."

"The UK purchasing managers is unambiguously strong and must be seen as increasing the risk of a BOE tightening at the end of the week. All of the components showed solid gains and both of the key price elements were too high for comfort. Since services is a much more important sector of the economy than manufacturing this report should be seen as a better guide to overall economic performance. It is likely to carry more weight at the MPC than its manufacturing sister survey."
